message:
fix(viewer): the saturation episode holds its own bounds -- no growth from failed candidates, no stale-iterator erase, sequence-wide floor and retirement

The verifying Claude found six boundary defects in the episode, all of them real; the pre-fix run
fails three assertions and then crashes, which is the iterator defect below.

A candidate that runs out of time inside an episode was recorded as a new abandoned identity, so a
host whose keys keep failing grew the list without end -- twenty failures turned sixteen records
into thirty-six. Inside an episode that is another attempt at the same recovery: nothing is
recorded and the floor rises instead.

A third key replaced the oldest candidate without checking that it was newer, so a key that
arrived late (past the floor but older than both candidates) evicted one that was being repaired.
And the assembly iterator was taken before that erase and compared after it -- a deque, so
undefined behaviour. The admission now runs before the lookup and only a newer key takes a slot.

The floor and the retirement were keyed by generation, but the host's sequence is monotone for the
whole UDP session: a record made under an older generation could hold the list at the cap and keep
blocking P frames after a new generation's IDR had been accepted. Both are sequence-wide now.

The delivered-candidate list grew whenever the final gate refused a completed key; it is a bounded
ring, and a key pushed out of it can no longer end the episode -- conservative, and no identity is
forgotten by it. Entering an episode trimmed only the non-key assemblies, so the two-slot bound
was violated from the start; the key assemblies are trimmed too, oldest first, raising the floor.
A release that keeps the latch now keeps the floor with it.

Each case asserts product state directly, and the test reports every case instead of stopping at
the first failure. history #425.
